chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan said:
I heard Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The time for Maghrib is when the sun sets and its disk disappears.'

He said: And I heard him saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) delayed the last 'Isha prayer one night as much as Allah willed. 'Umar came and knocked on the door and said: O Messenger of Allah, the women have slept, the children have slept. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came out and said: "You are not to annoy me, nor to command me; rather, upon you is to listen and obey."'

key_terms.تَسْمَعُوا وَ تُطِيعُوا: Listen and obey (a command to submit to authority)
key_terms.قُرْصُهَا: Its disk (referring to the sun's disk)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Maghrib prayer time and the meaning of 'Listen and obey' in the context of delaying prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* precisely defines the onset of Maghrib as the disappearance of the sun's disk, a standard criterion in Shia fiqh. It further illustrates the Prophet’s flexibility in delaying 'Isha, using the incident with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab to emphasize that while the leader may adjust timing, the community's primary duty is to listen and obey without causing him distress or demanding immediate action.
